Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we appreciate you making time. I'm Jordan Lee, AE for Redwood Partnerships, and with me is Priya, our systems engineer.
[00:18] Carlos: Thanks, Jordan. I'm Carlos, CTO at MapleGrid. Aisha and Liam are here too. We run a reseller/cloud integrator model and we've been getting more requests from enterprise customers to support hybrid GPU routing — like some inference in cloud, some on-prem for data residency.
[00:34] Priya: Cool, yeah that's exactly the pattern we've seen. Quick question to start — what's your primary ask? Is this a channel/reseller enablement or do you want a joint installed base pilot?
[00:48] Aisha: Mostly channel enablement right now, we want to understand the technical fit so we can start packaging it with our managed on-prem offering. But we also have one customer that might go to pilot — they'd need private networking and KMS integration.
[01:05] Liam: And just to add, our SREs want predictable latency. If we route to hosted sometimes we need fallbacks to local, and autoscaling behaviour matters.
[01:15] Jordan: Great, that helps. Priya, do you want to walk through the high-level topology options?
[01:22] Priya: Sure, briefly. Redwood supports three deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated pools (reserved capacity), and private deployment (VPC or on-prem). For channel partners like MapleGrid the typical pattern is hybrid routing: control plane in Redwood hosted, data plane either dedicated pools in a partner region or a private on-prem runtime.
[01:40] Priya: There are a few levers: routing by policy (latency first vs cost first), model variants for fallbacks (smaller quantized models for edge), and caching/prefix KV cache to cut token cost and reduce latency.
[01:56] Carlos: When you say dedicated pools, are those something we can run in our DCs or is that Redwood-managed in cloud regions?
[02:03] Priya: Dedicated can be either Redwood-managed in cloud regions or we ship a private runtime that you can run on-prem. For reseller setups, many partners prefer Redwood Private with a lightweight control plane so they can keep the inference traffic local but still get rollout/metrics.
[02:20] Aisha: Security question — what's the KMS story? Some of our finance customers specifically require HSM-backed keys and audit logs for model inputs.
[02:28] Jordan: Yep, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private installs and can surface audit logs for requests. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS summary doc after.
[02:37] Liam: Do you have SAML SSO and RBAC for multiple tenant separation? We need to map to our RBAC model.
[02:44] Priya: We do SAML SSO, SSO provisioning, and RBAC controls. For partner-managed deployments we also support per-tenant routing policies and per-customer billing tags so you can reconcile usage.
[03:01] Carlos: Ok good. From a technical constraints perspective, our biggest customers are sensitive to latency < 60ms p95 for short chat/embedding use cases. They'll tolerate higher for long-form generation but we need to be able to guarantee SLOs or at least fallback behaviours.
[03:19] Priya: Understood. We typically design routing policies with latency SLOs + a fallback path to a smaller model or local cache. For embeddings chat, KV cache + batching helps a lot. We can show token-level traces in the Console for debugging.
[03:33] Jordan: How about pilot scope — what would you need to validate before committing to a partner integration?
[03:39] Carlos: We want a 3-week pilot on our N8 cluster (on-prem) against a staged customer workload: throughput targets, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens. Also security review.
[03:48] Aisha: Procurement timeline is tight — Q4 decision ideally. We need pricing that supports a reseller margin and clear engineering runbook.
[03:57] Priya: For the benchmark, we'll need access to a test endpoint and a short runbook: model versions, quantization configs (we can test 8-bit and 4-bit), and load scripts. Also, a shared drive for results.
[04:12] Jordan: We'll prepare a partner runbook + pricing model. We'll also include suggestions on quantization profiles and expected throughput per GPU type.
[04:20] Liam: Quick practical Q — how do you handle KV cache invalidation when you have split routing between cloud and on-prem? We worry about stale context.
[04:29] Priya: Good point. Our approach is prefix-aware caching: request routing includes a cache affinity key and TTLs. For strong consistency you can route all cache-sensitive requests to the same locality. Otherwise, we use eventual invalidation and versioned keys. We can show a diagram in the runbook.
[04:46] Carlos: Are there any known blockers for connecting to our private network? VPC peering, private link, or do you use a control-plane tunnel?
[04:54] Priya: Options: VPC peering (cloud), PrivateLink, or a lightweight control-plane proxy for on-prem. For air-gapped installs we deploy a private control plane and local runtime; for partner-managed hybrid we can do secure tunnels and mTLS.
[05:09] Aisha: From a legal/compliance perspective, do you support data residency? Some customers mandate that model inputs never leave country boundaries.
[05:17] Jordan: Yes, with the private deployment and region pinning we can ensure traffic stays in-region and we can disable cloud fallbacks for those tenants. We'll document that in the runbook.
[05:25] Carlos: Pricing — can you share a sample reseller pricing tier? We need per-GPU throughput pricing and a margin table.
[05:32] Jordan: We'll send a partner pricing sheet. For pilots we often do a discounted committed-period pricing and then move to reserved capacity pricing for scale.
[05:40] Priya: Operationally, for a joint customer we recommend: 1) small benchmark, 2) a canary rollout with traffic split 90/10, 3) monitor token-level latency traces, 4) flip to local fallback if p95 exceeds threshold.
[05:56] Liam: For canary and A/B, do you support automatic fallback if a model variant degrades?
[06:02] Priya: Yes, we have automatic fallback policies — model variant fallback or regional fallback. It'll automatically route to a compatible variant if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.
[06:12] Carlos: Any gotchas with quantized models? Do you see quality regressions?
[06:17] Priya: There's always a tradeoff — 8-bit mostly fine for embeddings and many chat tasks; 4-bit can introduce artifacts for some instruction-following behavior. Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest profiles by workload and run evaluation tests.
[06:33] Aisha: Last one from me — what metrics do you need from our side to instrument success?
[06:38] Priya: Token throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rate, request distribution by tenant, and model version. Also, a small set of prompt-based quality checks for regressions.
[06:50] Jordan: Ok, let's recap. Actions: Priya will draft a benchmark plan; I'll share the partner runbook + pricing; Carlos will confirm time windows and stakeholders. We'll target the benchmark week of Oct 26th and have the pricing to you before that.
[07:04] Carlos: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[07:08] Liam: Nothing else. We'll pull procurement in after we see the benchmark plan.
[07:12] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone, we will follow up with links to the runbook and SOC2/KMS docs.
[07:18] Aisha: Thanks — appreciate it.
[07:20] Jordan: Meeting adjourned.
